title: Reliable pharmacy data at scale
subtitle: AWS · Snowflake · dbt · Airflow | Professional project summary
problem: Pharmacy-benefit, medication-adherence, formulary, and clinical-quality data needed reliable daily processing for analytics and regulatory reporting. Quality checks and PHI controls were central to the workflow.
role: Developed Python and PySpark ETL, modeled pharmacy analytics with dbt, orchestrated refreshes with Airflow, implemented validation, and tuned processing performance.
stages: Production Python and PySpark ETL processed 5–10 million pharmacy and clinical-quality records daily. AWS Glue extraction was coordinated through Airflow.
Delta Lake medallion layers organized raw ingestion, standardization and validation, and curated analytics datasets. PySpark performed transformations before downstream modeling.
Great Expectations and dbt tests checked schema, completeness, NDC format, formulary tiers, referential integrity, and business rules before production promotion.

Modular Snowflake dbt models separated pharmacy business logic for adherence, formulary utilization, drug costs, and clinical quality. SQL, clustering-key, and dbt optimization reduced warehouse compute costs by 25%; Athena queried curated S3 datasets.

Orchestrated 40+ Airflow DAGs, raising refresh SLA compliance from 88% to 99.2%. Partition tuning and incremental materialization reduced processing time by 30%. Dependency checks and alerts supported recovery; Docker and GitHub Actions supported tests and deployments.
quality: Great Expectations and dbt checks for schema, completeness, NDC format, formulary tier, and business rules
Referential-integrity checks and reusable pharmacy transformations
Field-level PHI masking, column-level controls, and audit logging
Cited pharmacy-policy context for human review of RAG responses
operations: 40+ Airflow DAGs coordinating Glue, PySpark, and Snowflake dbt runs
Dependency checks and alerts for delayed refreshes and pipeline recovery
Docker-packaged Python jobs and GitHub Actions tests and deployments
Snowflake query, clustering-key, and dbt model optimization
outcomes: 99.2% pharmacy refresh SLA compliance, up from 88%
25% reduction in Snowflake warehouse compute costs
tradeoffs: Batch and streaming: daily refreshes served scheduled reporting; Kafka feeds supported near-real-time utilization tracking.
Layered data: Bronze, Silver, and Gold separated ingestion from standardized and curated datasets.
AI assistance: Bedrock and Claude supported documentation and validation work with human review and PHI safeguards.
explain: At Blue Cross Blue Shield, I built production data workflows for pharmacy benefits and clinical-quality analytics. The main challenge was processing large daily volumes while keeping the data reliable and protecting PHI.

The workflow used AWS S3 and Glue for ingestion, PySpark and Delta Lake for processing, and Snowflake with dbt for analytics models. Airflow coordinated the dependencies, refreshes, checks, and alerts.
I implemented schema, completeness, NDC, formulary, and business-rule validation using Great Expectations and dbt tests. I also applied PHI masking, column-level access controls, and audit logging.

I orchestrated 40+ Airflow DAGs and improved pharmacy refresh SLA compliance from 88% to 99.2%. Partition tuning and incremental materialization reduced processing time by 30%. Snowflake query, clustering-key, and dbt model optimization reduced warehouse compute costs by 25%. I packaged Python jobs with Docker and automated tests and deployments with GitHub Actions.

title: A lakehouse for rewards analytics
subtitle: Azure · Databricks · Delta Lake · Kafka | Professional project summary
problem: Card transactions, rewards redemptions, and member spending needed consistent cleansing and aggregation for rewards analytics, member reporting, and downstream business decisions.
role: Developed Python and PySpark ETL, built parameterized ADF workflows, organized Delta Lake layers, supported streaming feeds and Power BI datasets, and maintained controlled deployments.
stages: Python and PySpark ETL on Azure Databricks ingested card transactions, rewards redemptions, and member spending into ADLS.

Cleansing, deduplication, and business-rule transformations prepared data. Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers organized batch processing for daily spend and merchant-performance analytics. PySpark null, duplicate, and schema checks validated data before publication to Silver and Gold.

Built Spark Structured Streaming pipelines with Kafka on Azure Databricks, ingesting 1.2M+ card transaction events per hour into Delta Lake Bronze/Silver with sub-minute latency for rewards and fraud analytics.
ADF and Databricks workflows loaded curated data into Synapse, Azure SQL, and PostgreSQL. Power BI dashboards supported rewards-program performance and card-member analytics.

Spark repartitioning, liquid clustering, and query tuning reduced daily Databricks cluster execution time by 25%, lowering monthly Azure compute costs. Azure DevOps CI/CD supported deployments; Docker and GitHub Actions automated Python job tests and pipeline deployments.
quality: PySpark null, duplicate, and schema checks before publishing to Silver and Gold
SQL window functions, cleansing, and deduplication rules
Consistent Synapse and Azure SQL datasets for Power BI reporting
operations: Parameterized ADF and Databricks incremental workflows into Synapse, Azure SQL, and PostgreSQL
Azure DevOps CI/CD, Docker, and GitHub Actions tests and deployments
Spark repartitioning, liquid clustering, and query tuning
Agile collaboration on Power BI rewards and merchant dashboards
outcomes: 1.2M+ card transaction events ingested per hour
Sub-minute streaming latency into Delta Lake Bronze/Silver
25% reduction in daily Databricks cluster execution time
Validated curated datasets for rewards and merchant analytics
tradeoffs: Batch and streaming: Spark batch jobs aggregated daily spend; Kafka supported faster transaction analytics.
Layered storage: medallion layers made raw, cleaned, and analytics-ready datasets easier to maintain.
Incremental loading: parameterized ADF workflows reduced repeated manual processing and accelerated data availability.
explain: At American Express, I worked on data pipelines for card transactions, rewards redemptions, and member spending. The goal was to provide consistent data for rewards analytics and timely loyalty reporting.

I built Python and PySpark pipelines on Azure Databricks and published clean datasets through Delta Lake Bronze, Silver, and Gold. Spark Structured Streaming and Kafka ingested 1.2M+ events per hour into Bronze/Silver with sub-minute latency.
ADF and Databricks workflows loaded curated data into Synapse, Azure SQL, and PostgreSQL. I also worked on Kafka transaction feeds and Power BI datasets for rewards and card-member analytics.

I reduced daily Databricks cluster execution time by 25% through Spark repartitioning, liquid clustering, and query tuning. Parameterized ADF and Databricks workflows automated incremental loads; Azure DevOps, Docker, and GitHub Actions supported controlled testing and deployments.

title: Trusted lending data foundations
subtitle: AWS · Redshift · Airflow · Power BI | Professional project summary
problem: Loan origination, credit risk, borrower, and performance data needed reliable delivery into a reporting warehouse. Source and warehouse figures needed reconciliation for useful lending and portfolio analytics.
role: Built production ETL, orchestrated extraction and loading, designed dimensional models, implemented reconciliation scripts, and supported portfolio dashboards and ETL deployment workflows.
stages: Python and PySpark ETL extracted loan origination, credit-risk, and borrower data from PostgreSQL into AWS S3 and Redshift.

Organized raw and curated loan data in AWS S3 with partitioned layouts and Glue Data Catalog tables. Glue crawlers supported schema discovery and catalog maintenance, efficient queries, and reliable downstream Redshift loads.
Redesigned Redshift dimensional schemas using Kimball methodology and tuned distribution and sort keys across 15+ fact and dimension tables, improving portfolio query execution times by 40%.
Automated loan-count and balance reconciliation in Python between PostgreSQL sources and the warehouse, supporting reliable lending and portfolio reporting.

Airflow orchestrated daily Glue extractions and Redshift loads with 99.5% pipeline uptime, delivering underwriting and portfolio risk reports 2 hours earlier each morning. Jenkins supported CI/CD and Power BI served reporting.
quality: Glue schema discovery and catalog maintenance
Consistent warehouse models for portfolio reporting
operations: Airflow dependencies and operational alerts for daily Glue and Redshift loads
99.5% pipeline uptime and underwriting SLA delivery
Source-to-target design documentation for reconciliation, audit traceability, and handoff
outcomes: 40% improvement in portfolio query execution times
15+ fact and dimension tables tuned with distribution and sort keys
Underwriting and portfolio risk reports delivered 2 hours earlier each morning
tradeoffs: Dimensional modeling: facts and business dimensions organized reporting around loans, performance, and borrower segments.
Reconciliation: counts and balances checked warehouse completeness against source data.
Orchestration: dependencies and alerts made daily report delivery easier to manage.
explain: At BHG Financial, I built data workflows for lending and credit-risk analytics. We needed loan origination, borrower, and performance data in a reliable reporting warehouse.
I developed Python and PySpark pipelines into AWS S3 and Redshift. Airflow coordinated AWS Glue extraction and warehouse loading with dependency management and operational alerts.

I redesigned Redshift dimensional schemas using Kimball methodology and tuned distribution and sort keys across 15+ fact and dimension tables, improving portfolio query execution times by 40%. Python reconciled loan counts and balances against PostgreSQL sources.

Airflow DAGs coordinated Glue extraction and Redshift loading with 99.5% pipeline uptime. Underwriting and portfolio risk reports were delivered 2 hours earlier each morning. I also documented source-to-target design decisions for audits and team handoff.
